title: Baba Bakala
hook: where Makhan Shah found the ninth Guru

segments.voice: Yesterday, Tarn Taran, Guru Arjan's wide pool, and a look back down the week's road. Your line was a wide pool. Who did you make room for? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-eight.

A man is standing on a rooftop in a village, shouting at the top of his lungs to everyone below: the Guru is found! The Guru is found! Down in the lanes, people stop and look up. A few of them are not happy to hear it. The village is Bakala, near the Beas. The man on the roof is a trader named Makhan Shah. And the one he found was not the loudest man in the village. He was the one sitting quietly. Today, the place where that happened.
screen: `A MAN ON A ROOFTOP.` → `THE GURU IS FOUND!` → `NOT THE LOUDEST. THE QUIET ONE.`

segments.voice: First, a riddle of two words. Tradition says the child Guru, Guru Har Krishan, as he was dying in Delhi, was asked who would come after him. He answered only: Baba Bakale. The Baba is in Bakala. Second, the crowd. Tradition says that when word spread, many men in Bakala set up seats and called themselves the Guru, each with his own followers and his own claims. It was noisy, and it was confusing. Third, the test. We've met Makhan Shah before, as a trader. Tradition says that in a storm at sea he had made a promise of an offering to the Guru if his ship came through. Arriving in Bakala, he didn't know whom to give it to, so he went from seat to seat, leaving each claimant a small gift and saying nothing of his promise. They took it, and thanked him. Then he came to Tegh Bahadur, a man who, tradition says, spent long hours in quiet meditation in a small room below ground. And Tegh Bahadur reminded him of the full promise he had made. That's when Makhan Shah ran up to the roof. Fourth, the teaching underneath. Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, later wrote hymns that are in the Guru Granth Sahib. In one, he says, in paraphrase: holy people, give up the pride of the mind. The one who was found had not been looking to be found. Today a gurdwara stands at Baba Bakala, and Sikhs visit the place tradition remembers as that underground room.
screen: `BABA BAKALE: A TWO-WORD RIDDLE.` · `MANY SEATS, MANY CLAIMS.` · `THE PROMISE REMEMBERED.` · `GIVE UP THE PRIDE OF THE MIND.` · then, large: `THE GURU FOUND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look past the loudest voice. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a room you were in recently: a meeting, a family dinner, a group chat. Notice who took up the most space. Now let that voice fade a little, and look around the room for the quiet one. The person who said one thing, or nothing. What were they noticing? What did they know that nobody asked about? Stay with them for a few breaths. The bell holds the time.
Baba Bakala. The village near the Beas where, tradition says, Makhan Shah found Guru Tegh Bahadur among many claimants, and shouted it from the roof. Today's word.
Your line: the guru found. Today, in one conversation, ask the quietest person what they think, and listen to the whole answer. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-eight.

howItsDone: Sikhs visit Gurdwara Baba Bakala Sahib and the place tradition remembers as Guru Tegh Bahadur's room of meditation, and they tell the story of Makhan Shah, especially around the ninth Guru's gurpurab.
